title: In-Product Event Envelope
description: Contract for events emitted from inside the authenticated product, by the application backend or the app client. Unlike the marketing-site data layer, these events are emitted directly to the collection endpoint rather than through window.dataLayer, because the browser is not a trustworthy narrator of what the product actually did.

event_id.description: Deduplication key. For server events derived from a database transaction, deriving this deterministically from (table, row_id, transition) makes the whole pipeline idempotent under replay.

event_ts.description: When the transition occurred, not when it was dispatched. For batched or queued emission these differ, and using dispatch time silently smears your funnels.

ingested_ts.description: Set by the collection endpoint. event_ts minus ingested_ts is your pipeline latency SLI.

emitter.description: Which system emitted this. Tier 0 events MUST NOT come from a *_client emitter.

is_backfill.description: True for historical replays. Every downstream metric must be able to exclude backfills, or a migration will look like a growth spike.

identity.description: Account-first by design. In B2B the account is the unit that renews, expands and churns; a user-scoped retention curve on a B2B product is a vanity chart.

actor_type.description: support_impersonation MUST be excluded from every product metric. Failing to model this means your support team's activity inflates your engagement numbers.

feature.description: Present on feature_used / feature_configured / feature_adopted / feature_abandoned. feature_id is validated against the registry in tooling/tracking-plan.json.

usage_depth.description: The depth ladder. A feature with high 'viewed' and near-zero 'configured' has an activation problem, not a demand problem.

usage_index.description: Nth use by this user. Removes the need for a separate first_used event: usage_index = 1 IS the first-use cohort.

onboarding.description: Present on the onboarding_* family. The generic step model: one event family, any number of steps, no schema change when the flow is reordered.

flow_version.description: Completion rates are never compared across flow_version values without an explicit annotation. A version change means the denominator changed.

reliability.description: Present on error and performance events. Never carries a raw error message or stack trace: those leak user content and belong in the error monitor, which is a different system under a different legal basis.

endpoint_pattern.description: Templated path such as /v1/workspaces/{id}/items. NEVER the populated path: real paths carry identifiers and blow up cardinality.

is_user_facing.description: Whether a human saw this fail. Separates the support queue from the engineering page.

governance.description: Metadata carried for lineage and compliance. Written by the collection layer from tracking-plan.json, never by the emitting application.

tier.description: 0 revenue/contractual, 1 activation loop, 2 feature usage, 3 experimental.

contains_pii.description: Asserted false and enforced. An event carrying PII must not reach this pipeline at all.
